question: Why put an in-process cache in front of a DB query or a service call, and why is a plain Map with setTimeout not enough?
answer_hinglish:
Cache ka kaam simple hai: jo kaam baar baar repeat ho raha hai -- same DB query, same doosri service ki HTTP call, same config lookup -- uska result memory mein rakh lo aur agli baar wahi se de do. PLAN.md ka point yahi hai: zyada tar backend latency repeated work hai, aur ek DB query typically millisecond ke order ki hoti hai, jabki memory se read uske saamne bahut sasta hai.

Par naive version -- ek `Map` plus `setTimeout` -- teen nayi problems laata hai, aur cache-kit inhi ko solve karta hai. Pehli: Map bina limit ke badhta rehta hai, toh process memory se bahar chala jaata hai. Isliye `maxEntries` REQUIRED hai, aur optional `maxWeight` bytes ki doosri limit hai. Doosri: expired value serve ho jaati hai ya har key ke liye ek timer chalta hai. Yahan lazy expiry hai -- har read expiry check karta hai, expired value kabhi return nahi hoti. Teesri: cold key par 100 requests ek saath aayi toh 100 identical queries DB par jaati hain (cache stampede). `getOrLoad` mein single flight hai: loader ek hi baar chalta hai.

Uske upar stage 2 mein stale-while-revalidate, negative caching aur ek optional Redis L2 hai. Library ka koi runtime dependency nahi hai aur koi framework import nahi karta, toh same code Express handler, NestJS service, worker ya script mein chalta hai. Interview mein main yeh bolunga: caching ka faayda obvious hai, asli engineering un failure modes mein hai jo naive cache laata hai.
why_needed: Repeated kaam (same query, same call) latency aur DB load dono badhata hai. Cache usse hatata hai -- par bina bound, bina expiry aur bina stampede protection ke cache khud ek outage ka source ban jaata hai.
real_world_analogy: Office ke paas wali chai ki dukaan: har baar door wali factory se chai mangwane ki jagah ek flask bhar ke rakh lo. Par flask ki size limited hai, thandi chai phenkni padti hai, aur jab flask khaali ho toh 10 log alag alag factory na bhaagein -- ek jaaye, baaki wait karein.
how_it_works: Caller `getOrLoad(key, loader)` bulata hai. Live fresh entry mili toh turant value (hit). Nahi mili toh loader chalta hai, result store hota hai TTL ke saath, aur limits cross hone par least recently used entry nikal di jaati hai.
in_this_project: README ka 'Use it' example: `new LruCache<string, User | null>({ maxEntries: 10_000, maxWeight: 50 * 1024 * 1024, weigh: (u) => Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(u)), ttlMs: 60_000, sweepIntervalMs: 30_000, onEvent })`. Ek cache per KIND of data, module level par ek baar banta hai. `updateUser` DB update ke baad `users.delete(id)` karta hai. Status: 178 tests (stage 3 tak), npm par publish nahi hai.

Memory bounded (maxEntries required)
Stampede protection built in
Framework-free, zero runtime dependencies

Har process ka apna cache: replicas ke beech consistency nahi (uske liye TwoLevelCache)
Ek aur cheez jise tune karna padta hai (TTL, limits)

Bina limit ka Map ko cache bolna
Update ke baad cache delete bhool jaana

question: What is LRU eviction, and why is maxEntries a required option in cache-kit?
answer_hinglish:
LRU yaani Least Recently Used: jab cache full ho jaaye aur nayi entry aaye, toh woh entry nikaalo jise sabse lamba time se kisi ne use nahi kiya. Assumption yeh hai ki jo recently use hua woh dobara use hone ke chances zyada hain (temporal locality). Ek popular user ka record baar baar padha jaata hai, toh woh end par rehta hai aur bachta hai; ek baar padhi gayi purani entry front par khisak jaati hai aur pehle nikalti hai.

cache-kit mein `maxEntries` required hai -- constructor mein `Number.isSafeInteger(maxEntries) && maxEntries >= 1` check hota hai, warna `RangeError`. Code comment seedha bolta hai: 'an unbounded cache is a memory leak with extra steps'. PLAN.md bhi yahi kehta hai: bina bound ka cache ek slow memory leak hai -- production mein dheere dheere heap bharta hai aur ek din process OOM se marta hai, aur kisi ko pata nahi chalta kyun.

Rule exact hai: exactly `maxEntries` par kuch evict nahi hota; ek aur entry aaye tab least recently used jaata hai (event `evict` with reason `size`). Existing key par `set` replace karta hai -- entry most recent ho jaati hai, TTL restart, koi eviction nahi. Yeh boundary test mein dono taraf se locked hai, aur mutation checks L3 / L4 (off by one dono directions) pakde gaye. Interview mein bolna: LRU ek heuristic hai, perfect nahi -- ek bada scan hot keys ko nikaal sakta hai (LFU / W-TinyLFU admission yahan implement nahi hai).
why_needed: Bina limit ke cache memory leak hai. Limit lagani padegi, aur limit par kisko nikaalna hai uska ek simple, sasta rule chahiye -- LRU wahi hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek chhoti bookshelf jisme 10 kitaabein aati hain. Jo kitaab padhte ho woh right end par rakh dete ho. Nayi kitaab aaye aur jagah na ho, toh left end wali (sabse purani padhi) hata do.
how_it_works: Har hit key ko order ke end par le jaata hai. Store ke baad `while (map.size > maxEntries) evictOldest("size")` -- order ke start wali key nikalti hai.
in_this_project: `LruCache` constructor maxEntries validate karta hai. `store()` mein eviction loop. `test/lru.test.ts` ka 'exactly at maxEntries nothing is evicted; one more evicts the least recently used': maxEntries 3, a/b/c set, koi event nahi; `set("d")` ke baad keys `["b","c","d"]` aur ek event `{ type: "evict", key: "a", reason: "size" }`. 'maxEntries 1 keeps only the last key' bhi test hai.

Hot keys naturally bachti hain
Memory hamesha bounded
disadvantages: Ek bada one-time scan hot keys ko nikaal sakta hai
Frequency nahi dekhta, sirf recency
common_mistakes: maxEntries optional rakhna 'kyunki abhi data kam hai'
Off-by-one: limit par hi evict kar dena

question: What does a TTL mean in cache-kit, and what is lazy expiry?
answer_hinglish:
TTL (time to live) matlab entry kitni der tak valid hai. cache-kit mein rule exact hai: entry time t par `ttlMs` 100 ke saath set hui toh woh t + 99 par live hai aur t + 100 par EXPIRED -- 'AT', 'after' nahi. TTL `set` se count hota hai, last read se nahi (sliding expiry implement nahi hai). Cache-wide `ttlMs` default hai, per-entry `set(key, value, { ttlMs })` usse override karta hai, `Infinity` matlab kabhi expire nahi, aur koi TTL na do toh entry expire hi nahi hoti (sirf LRU nikaalega).

Lazy expiry ka matlab: koi timer har entry ke liye nahi chalta. Jab bhi `get`, `peek`, `has`, `delete` ya `getOrLoad` kisi key ko chhoote hain, woh expiry check karte hain; expired entry wahin remove hoti hai (`evict` event, reason `expired`) aur kabhi return nahi hoti. Isliye correctness ke liye timer ki zaroorat hi nahi.

Catch: jo expired entry koi padhta hi nahi, woh memory mein padi rehti hai -- `size` usse count karta hai. README 'Known' mein yeh honestly likha hai. Uske liye optional `sweepIntervalMs` hai jo `purgeExpired()` chalata hai, ya woh entry eviction victim banke nikal jaati hai. Interview mein point: correctness (expired value kabhi nahi milti) aur memory reclaim (sweep) do alag concerns hain, aur cache-kit unhe alag rakhta hai.
why_needed: Data badalta hai; TTL upper bound deta hai ki cache kitna purana data de sakta hai. Lazy check se yeh guarantee bina kisi timer ke milti hai.
real_world_analogy: Dudh ke packet par expiry date: fridge khud packet nahi phenkta, par jab bhi tum nikaalte ho date dekh lete ho aur expired ho toh phenk dete ho.
how_it_works: Entry store hote waqt `expiresAt = now() + ttl` (ya Infinity). Read par `now() >= deadAt` ho toh evict as expired; stale grace ke bina `deadAt === expiresAt`.
in_this_project: `store()` expiresAt calculate karta hai; private `live()` mein `if (this.now() >= entry.deadAt) { this.evict(key, "expired"); return undefined; }`. `test/ttl.test.ts`: 'boundary: live 1 ms before ttlMs, expired AT ttlMs', 'get does not extend the TTL (expiry counts from set)', 'set again restarts the TTL', aur expired entry ke liye `size` pehle 1 phir read ke baad 0. Mutation T1 (live AT expiresAt) pakda gaya.

Expired value kabhi return nahi hoti
Boundary ek rule, dono taraf tested
disadvantages: Unread expired entries memory lete hain jab tak sweep / eviction na ho
`size` mein expired entries bhi count hoti hain

question: What is the difference between get, peek and has in LruCache?
answer_hinglish:
Teeno key ko dekhte hain, par side effects alag hain -- aur yahi fark interview mein poocha jaata hai.

`get(key)` ek 'real read' hai: fresh entry mili toh `hits` +1 aur key most recently used ban jaati hai (Map se delete karke dobara insert); nahi mili toh `misses` +1 aur `undefined`. `peek(key)` sirf dekhta hai: value deta hai par recency nahi badalta aur stats nahi chhoota. `has(key)` bhi recency aur stats nahi chhoota, bas boolean deta hai. Code comment `peek` ke upar likha hai: 'No recency change, no stats.'

Peek kyun chahiye? Debugging, metrics, ya admin endpoint jo cache ke andar jhaankta hai -- agar woh `get` use kare toh har jhaank ek key ko 'hot' bana dega aur hit ratio bigaad dega. `has` isliye bhi useful hai kyunki value `undefined` store ho sakti hai: test 'an undefined value is stored: has() tells it apart from a miss' dikhata hai ki `get` dono case mein `undefined` deta hai, `has` fark batata hai.

Teen common cheezein: teeno expired entry ko return nahi karte (aur use lazily remove karte hain); teeno stale entry (TTL ke baad, grace ke andar) ko bhi absent maante hain -- woh sirf `getOrLoad` ke liye rakhi jaati hai. Hits aur misses sirf `get` aur `getOrLoad` se count hote hain.
why_needed: Cache ko inspect karna aur cache ko use karna alag cheezein hain. Inspect karne se LRU order aur hit ratio nahi badalna chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Library mein kitaab issue karna (get) vs shelf par dekh lena ki hai ya nahi (has) vs kitaab ka pehla page wahi khade khade padh lena (peek) -- sirf issue karne se register mein entry hoti hai.
how_it_works: `get` -> `fresh()` -> mila toh `hit()` (counter + `touch()` = delete + set). `peek` -> `fresh(key)?.value`. `has` -> `fresh(key) !== undefined`.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts mein teeno methods 3-8 lines ke hain aur sab private `fresh()` par based. `test/lru.test.ts` 'peek and has do NOT change recency': a/b/c ke baad peek(a), has(a), phir set(d) -> a nikal jaata hai. `test/stats-events.test.ts` 'hits and misses come from get and getOrLoad only (not peek / has)' poora stats object compare karta hai. Mutation L1 (`get` recency refresh nahi karta) 10 tests ne pakda.

question: What does stats() report, and why are hits and misses counters instead of events?
answer_hinglish:
`stats()` ek copy return karta hai counters ki -- `{ ...this.counters, evictions: { ...this.counters.evictions } }` -- toh caller usse badal bhi de toh cache ke counters safe hain (test 'stats() is a copy'). Fields: `hits`, `misses` (sirf `get` aur `getOrLoad` se), `loads` (loader calls), `coalesced` (miss jo already running load mein join hua), `loadErrors` (aborted loads count nahi hote), `rejected` (maxWeight se bhaari values), aur `evictions: { size, weight, expired }`. Stage 2 ne add kiye: `staleHits`, `negativeHits` (hits ka part), `refreshes` (loads ka part), `refreshErrors` (loadErrors ka part). Code comment ke hisaab se `staleHits` na hit hai na miss.

Hits / misses event kyun nahi? Kyunki woh HAR call par hote hain. Agar har read ek `onEvent` callback chalaye toh har read ka cost badhega -- jo cache ki hot path hai. Events un cheezon ke liye hain jo cache 'khud se' karta hai: evict, reject, load, load-error, load-abort, refresh, refresh-error. PLAN.md: 'Stats are counters, events are for things the cache does by itself'.

Production mein pattern: ek metrics endpoint `stats()` expose kare (README: `app.get("/metrics/cache", ...)`), Prometheus scrape karke rate nikaale, hit ratio = hits / (hits + misses). `evictions.size` tezi se badh raha hai toh cache chhota hai; `expired` zyada hai toh TTL chhota hai ya data cold hai.
why_needed: Cache bina metrics ke andha hai: hit ratio, eviction reason aur load errors ke bina pata hi nahi chalta ki cache kaam kar raha hai ya sirf memory kha raha hai.
real_world_analogy: Gaadi ka odometer vs warning light: odometer (counter) har km chupchaap badhta hai, warning light (event) sirf tab jalti hai jab kuch khaas hua.
how_it_works: Private `counters` object har operation mein increment hota hai. `stats()` shallow copy plus evictions ki copy deta hai.
in_this_project: `CacheStats` interface src/cache.ts mein har field ka comment rakhta hai. `test/stats-events.test.ts` exact object compare karta hai: ek set, get hit, get miss, peek/has, ek getOrLoad hit aur ek miss ke baad `hits: 2, misses: 2, loads: 1`. 'an expired entry read by get is a miss': `misses: 1, evictions: { expired: 1 }`. Mutation E3 (`stats()` live counters return kare) pakda gaya.

Eviction reasons alag alag dikhte hain

question: What is stale-while-revalidate, and what are the fresh, stale and gone windows in cache-kit?
answer_hinglish:
Stale-while-revalidate (SWR) ka idea: TTL khatam hone par user ko DB ka wait mat karwao; purani value turant de do aur background mein EK refresh chala do. Agli request ko nayi value milegi.

cache-kit mein entry ke paas do timestamps hain: `expiresAt` (fresh time ka end) aur `deadAt = expiresAt + staleMs`. Example (README): t par set, `ttlMs` 100, `staleMs` 50 -> [t, t+100) FRESH, [t+100, t+150) STALE, t+150 se GONE (lazily removed as `expired`). `staleMs` cache-wide, per `set`, ya per `getOrLoad` call ho sakta hai; default 0 matlab koi grace nahi aur stage 1 behaviour bilkul same.

Stale window mein `getOrLoad` purani value TURANT return karta hai (`staleHits` +1, key most recent), aur agar us key ka koi load already nahi chal raha toh ek background refresh shuru karta hai (`refresh` event, `refreshes` +1, loader ke context mein `refresh: true`). 50 concurrent stale reads -> 1 loader call (tested). Gone ke baad yeh normal miss hai: caller loader ka wait karta hai.

Important: `get` / `peek` / `has` stale entry KABHI return nahi karte. Unke paas loader nahi hai, refresh shuru nahi kar sakte; stale return karte toh `ttlMs` ka matlab hi khatam ho jaata. Stale data chahiye toh `getOrLoad` use karo.
why_needed: TTL boundary par har popular key ek latency spike deti hai (sab DB ka wait karte hain). SWR woh spike hata deta hai, aur grace period ek slow ya failing backend ko 'ride out' karne deta hai.
real_world_analogy: Akhbaar wala: aaj ka akhbaar late hai toh woh kal ka nahi phenkta -- 'abhi yeh padh lo, naya aa raha hai' bolke kal wala de deta hai, aur ek hi aadmi press bhejta hai naya laane.
how_it_works: `getOrLoad`: `live()` (deadAt se pehle) mila; `now < expiresAt` toh hit; warna stale -> `staleHits++`, touch, `if (!this.flights.has(key)) this.startLoad(key, loader, options, true)`, aur purani value return.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts `Entry` mein `expiresAt` aur `deadAt`. `test/swr.test.ts` boundaries: 'at ttl - 1 the entry is fresh', 'AT ttl the entry is stale', 'at ttl + staleMs - 1 it is still served stale; AT ttl + staleMs it is gone: a miss that waits for the loader', '50 concurrent stale reads start ONE refresh'. Mutation R3 (koi grace nahi) 29 tests ne pakda, R5 (stale read refresh ka wait kare) 26 ne.

Ek refresh per key, stampede nahi
Backend slow / down ho toh grace tak purana data milta rehta hai
disadvantages: Grace mein data TTL se zyada purana ho sakta hai
Refresh fail ho toh retry agli stale read par, bina backoff
common_mistakes: get() se stale data expect karna

question: What is negative caching, and how does cache-kit decide what counts as 'not found'?
answer_hinglish:
Negative caching matlab 'yeh cheez exist nahi karti' wala answer bhi cache karna. Bina iske, missing id ka har lookup DB tak jaata hai -- ek bot jo random ids maar raha hai, ya ek deleted user jise sab dhoondh rahe hain, har request par ek query. cache-kit mein `negativeTtlMs` set karo toh ek LOADED value jiske liye `isNegative(value)` true hai (default: `null` ya `undefined`) `min(jo TTL use milta, negativeTtlMs)` ke liye store hoti hai, aur usse koi stale grace nahi milti.

Result (tested): missing id ke 1000 sequential + 100 concurrent lookups -> sirf 1 loader call. Negative entry par hit `hits` aur `negativeHits` dono mein count hota hai.

Teen design details: (1) Short TTL kyun -- missing cheez kabhi bhi create ho sakti hai (naya user signup), toh 'not found' ko lambe time tak yaad rakhna galat hoga. (2) Sirf LOADED values classify hoti hain: `set(key, null)` ek ordinary value hai, normal TTL ke saath, kyunki caller ne explicitly likha. (3) `isNegative` bina `negativeTtlMs` ke diya toh `TypeError` -- silently ignore hone wala option fail loudly karta hai.

Aur sabse important: ERRORS cache nahi hote, negative caching on ho tab bhi. Loader ne throw kiya toh woh 'not found' nahi hai; agla call phir load karega. Loader ko pata ho ki error ka matlab 404 hai toh woh `null` return kare.
why_needed: Missing keys ka flood (bots, deleted records) bina negative caching ke seedha DB par girta hai, kyunki cache mein kuch store hi nahi hota.
real_world_analogy: Receptionist ko bol do 'Sharma ji is building mein nahi baithte' -- 5 minute tak jo bhi pooche, woh turant mana kar de, har baar poori directory na khole. Par 5 minute baad dobara check kare, kya pata Sharma ji aa gaye.
how_it_works: Loaded value par `negativeOf(value)`; true ho toh `loadedTtl()` = `Math.min(ttlMs ?? Infinity, negativeTtlMs)`, stale 0, `negative: true` entry par flag. Hit par flag dekh ke `negativeHits++`.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts: constructor mein default `isNegative = (v) => v === undefined || v === null`; `loadedTtl()` cap lagata hai; `startLoad` mein `this.store(key, value, weight, this.loadedTtl(value, context.ttlMs), negative ? 0 : stale, negative)`. `test/negative.test.ts`: '1000 sequential + 100 concurrent -> ONE loader call', 'a negative entry gets no stale grace', 'set(key, null) is an explicit value', 'errors are still NOT cached'. TwoLevelCache bhi `loadedTtl` use karta hai taaki Redis copy same short TTL ke saath likhe.

question: How does cache-kit get O(1) LRU from a JavaScript Map instead of a linked list?
answer_hinglish:
JavaScript ka `Map` spec ke hisaab se keys ko insertion order mein iterate karta hai. Yahi LRU order ban jaata hai: Map ki PEHLI key least recently used hai, aakhri key most recently used. Kisi key ko 'recent' banana ho toh `map.delete(key)` phir `map.set(key, entry)` -- woh end par chali jaati hai. Teeno operations (get, set, delete) hash-table ke hain, toh average O(1).

cache-kit mein yeh private `touch()` hai, aur `hit()` (get / getOrLoad ka hit) aur stale hit dono isse call karte hain. Naya `set` bhi pehle `remove(key)` karta hai phir `map.set`, toh replace bhi end par jaata hai. Eviction victim Map ki pehli key hai -- par usse ek long-lived iterator se nikaala jaata hai (`this.oldest`), har baar `map.keys().next()` se nahi. Woh ek benchmark ne pakda tha (alag question hai).

`get`, `set`, `delete`, `peek`, `has` O(1) hain (evicting set amortized O(1)); `purgeExpired()` aur `keys()` O(n). PLAN.md ka decision: textbook answer doubly linked list + hash map hai, par yahan 'only adds code to get wrong' -- Map pehle se ordered hash map hai, node objects nahi banane padte. Interview mein yeh bolna strong hai: main textbook answer jaanta hoon, par runtime ka built-in data structure wahi guarantee deta hai, aur maine model test se order verify kiya.
why_needed: LRU ke liye do cheezein O(1) chahiye: key se lookup, aur order mein move-to-end / remove-first. Map dono deta hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank ki queue jahan har aadmi ka token number hai: koi wapas aaye toh line se nikal ke peeche lag jaata hai; counter hamesha line ke aage wale ko bulata hai.
how_it_works: Order = insertion order. Hit: delete + set (end par). Evict: iterator se pehli key. Replace: remove + set. Iterator deleted keys skip karta hai aur baad mein add hui keys visit karta hai (spec).
in_this_project: src/cache.ts class comment: 'LRU order is the Map's insertion order: the first key is the least recently used. A hit deletes and re-inserts the key, which moves it to the end.' `touch()` 2 lines ka hai. `keys()` debug ke liye `[...this.map.keys()]` least recent first deta hai. `test/model.test.ts` 8 seeds x 3000 steps mein har step ke baad `cache.keys()` ko ek naive array model se compare karta hai.

question: How do maxEntries and maxWeight work together, and what is weigh() for?
answer_hinglish:
Sirf entry count ki limit tab kaafi nahi jab values ka size bahut alag alag ho -- 10 000 entries mein kuch 100 bytes ki aur kuch 5 MB ki ho sakti hain. Isliye cache-kit mein optional doosri limit `maxWeight` hai, aur `weigh(value, key)` har value ka weight batata hai (jaise `Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(u))` bytes). `maxWeight` diya aur `weigh` nahi toh constructor `TypeError` deta hai.

`store()` ka order: pehle key ki purani entry remove (uska weight minus), phir naye ka weight plus, phir `while (map.size > maxEntries) evictOldest("size")`, phir `while (weightTotal > maxWeight && map.size > 1) evictOldest("weight")`. Matlab dono limits independently check hoti hain aur har eviction apna reason report karti hai. Exactly limit par (entries == maxEntries ya weight == maxWeight) kuch evict nahi hota.

Test example: maxWeight 10, 'aaaa' + 'bbb' + 'ccc' = 10, koi event nahi. `set("d", "dddddd")` -> total 16 -> a nikla (12) -> b nikla (9) -> fit. Dono limits wale test mein: maxEntries 2, maxWeight 5 -- pehle size wali evictions, phir weight wali, apne apne reason ke saath.

`weigh` bina `maxWeight` ke bhi chal sakta hai -- tab sirf `totalWeight` metric feed karta hai. Dhyan: `weigh` har `set` aur har loaded value par chalta hai, toh JSON.stringify bade object par write path ka cost hai (README 'Known').
why_needed: Count limit memory ko bound nahi karti agar values ka size variable hai. Bytes ki limit asli memory ke kareeb hai.
real_world_analogy: Truck mein 'max 20 boxes' bhi likha hai aur 'max 2 ton' bhi: 20 halke box chal jaayenge, par 5 bhaari box se hi weight limit aa jaayegi.
how_it_works: Running total `weightTotal` har store / remove par update hota hai. Eviction LRU order mein jab tak dono limits ke andar na aa jaaye.

question: What happens when a single value is heavier than maxWeight on its own, and why is the key's older value removed?
answer_hinglish:
Agar ek akeli value hi `maxWeight` se bhaari hai, toh cache-kit use STORE NAHI karta: `set` `false` return karta hai, ek `reject` event (key aur weight ke saath) aata hai, `stats().rejected` +1 hota hai, aur baaki kuch evict nahi hota. Aur ek subtle rule: us key ki PURANI value bhi hata di jaati hai.

Teen options the, PLAN.md ne ek choose kiya. (1) Store kar do: woh baaki sab entries nikaal degi aur PHIR BHI limit se upar rahegi -- cache poora khaali aur limit violated. (2) Purani value rakh lo: caller ne abhi abhi naya value set kiya hai, matlab purana galat hai; usse serve karna stale read hai. (3) Reject + purana hatao: limit kabhi violate nahi hoti aur koi stale value nahi milti. Teesra chosen.

Exactly `maxWeight` jitni value store hoti hai aur baaki sab ko bahar dhakel deti hai -- boundary test hai ('a value exactly maxWeight heavy is stored').

`getOrLoad` ke case mein: loaded value bahut bhaari hai toh caller ko value phir bhi milti hai (load ka kaam waste nahi), bas cache nahi hoti, aur `rejected` +1. Code mein yeh `store()` ki pehli lines hain: `this.remove(key)` pehle, phir `weight > maxWeight` check. Mutations W2 (reject nahi) aur W3 (purani value rakh li) dono 12 aur 10 tests ne pakde.
why_needed: Ek outlier value poore cache ko flush na kare, aur limit kabhi violate na ho -- aur replace ke baad purana data serve na ho.
real_world_analogy: Lift mein 'max 500 kg' hai aur ek 600 kg ka crate aaya: baaki logon ko utaar ke bhi woh fit nahi hoga, toh crate ko seedhi se bhejo. Aur jo purana crate uski jagah tha, woh ab outdated hai -- woh bhi hata do.
how_it_works: `store()`: `remove(key)` -> agar `maxWeight !== undefined && weight > maxWeight` -> `rejected++`, `reject` event, `return false`. Warna normal store aur eviction.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts `store()` aur `set()` ka comment: 'Returns false when the value was not stored because it alone is heavier than maxWeight; any older value for the key is removed in that case too'. `test/lru.test.ts` 'a single value heavier than maxWeight is not stored, evicts nothing, and removes the key's older value': `set("k","12345")` with maxWeight 4 -> false, `has("k")` false, events `[{ type: "reject", key: "k", weight: 5 }]`. `test/load.test.ts` 'a loaded value too heavy to store is still returned, but not cached'.

Outlier poore cache ko flush nahi karta
Stale read nahi
Reject observable hai (event + counter)
disadvantages: Woh key cache hi nahi hoti: har read loader tak jaayega
Caller ko return value check karni padti hai
common_mistakes: set() ka false return ignore karna
Purani value rakhna 'kuch toh mile' soch kar
maxWeight itna chhota rakhna ki normal values reject hon

question: What are the eviction reasons in cache-kit, and how is the reason chosen for a victim that is expired or stale?
answer_hinglish:
`EvictionReason` teen hain: `size` (maxEntries cross hua), `weight` (maxWeight cross hua), `expired` (entry apni grace ke bhi baad thi). Har eviction `evict` event (key + reason) aur `stats().evictions[reason]` +1 karta hai.

Subtle part: LRU victim ka reason kya ho? Rule `evictOldest()` mein hai: `this.evict(key, this.now() >= entry.deadAt ? "expired" : reason)`. Matlab agar victim pehle se dead tha (deadAt ke baad), toh use `expired` report karo, `size` / `weight` nahi -- kyunki woh limit ki wajah se nahi, expiry ki wajah se bekaar tha. Isse metrics honest rehte hain: `evictions.size` sirf un entries ko count kare jo abhi useful thi aur limit ne nikaali; warna tum sochoge cache chhota hai jabki asal mein TTL chhota hai.

Stage 2 mein stale entry (TTL ke baad, grace ke andar) ka kya? Woh abhi bhi `getOrLoad` ke liye usable thi, toh limit ka reason milta hai. Lazy read, `purgeExpired()` aur sweep sab `deadAt` use karte hain.

Kya eviction NAHI hai: explicit `delete()` aur `clear()` -- user ne khud hataya, toh koi event aur koi counter nahi (test 'explicit delete and clear are not evictions'). Replace (`set` existing key) bhi eviction nahi. Mutation T5 (expired victim ko size / weight report karo) 10 tests ne pakda, R13 (stale victim ko expired) bhi 10 ne.
why_needed: Eviction reason se hi tuning decision hota hai: size badhao, weight badhao, ya TTL dekho. Galat reason galat tuning karwata hai.
real_world_analogy: Godown se maal nikalna: jagah ki kami se nikala (size), floor ka load limit (weight), ya expiry date nikal gayi thi (expired). Expired dabba agar jagah ki kami ke time nikla, tab bhi register mein 'expired' likhna sahi hai.
how_it_works: Lazy read / purge: `now >= deadAt` -> `expired`. LRU victim: wahi check, warna limit ka reason. delete / clear private `remove()` use karte hain jo event nahi bhejta.
in_this_project: src/events.ts `export type EvictionReason = "size" | "weight" | "expired"`. src/cache.ts `evictOldest()` aur `evict()` vs `remove()`. Tests: `test/ttl.test.ts` 'an expired eviction victim is reported as expired, not as size'; `test/swr.test.ts` 'a stale eviction victim is reported with the limit's reason, a dead one as expired'; `test/stats-events.test.ts` 'explicit delete and clear are not evictions'. Model test aakhir mein check karta hai ki teeno reasons kam se kam 50 baar hit hue.
advantages: Metrics se sahi tuning signal
delete / clear metrics ko pollute nahi karte
Stale vs dead ka fark clear
disadvantages: Reason ek heuristic hai: victim choose LRU se hi hota hai, expired entries ko pehle nahi dhoondha jaata
common_mistakes: Explicit delete ko eviction count karna
Dead victim ko size count karke cache size badhate jaana
Stale entry ko expired maan lena
follow_up_questions: Should the cache prefer evicting an expired entry over the LRU one? What would it cost?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Victim selection pure LRU hai (O(1)); expired entries dhoondh ke pehle nikaalna O(n) scan ya ek alag expiry index (heap / timing wheel) maangta. Isliye sirf reporting honest hai, selection nahi badla.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar reason galat hota (expired ko size bolna), on-call engineer maxEntries badhata rehta jabki asli issue chhota TTL ya cold data hai -- memory badhti, hit ratio nahi.
advanced.alternatives: Expiry-ordered index (min-heap ya hierarchical timing wheel) jisse expired entries pehle evict hon; ya sweep ko frequent chalana. Caffeine timing wheel use karta hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Lakhon entries par per-event `onEvent` callback costly ho sakta hai (har eviction ek call) -- counters sasti hain, events ko sample ya aggregate karna padega. Reason logic khud O(1) hai.

question: What does the optional sweep (sweepIntervalMs) do, why is its timer unref'd, and what does close() do?
answer_hinglish:
Lazy expiry correctness deta hai, par jo expired entry koi padhta nahi woh memory mein padi rehti hai. Optional `sweepIntervalMs` us memory ko free karta hai: constructor ek `setInterval(() => this.purgeExpired(), every)` lagata hai, aur `purgeExpired()` saari entries walk karke jo `deadAt` cross kar chuki hain unhe `expired` reason ke saath nikaal deta hai (O(n), returns kitni hatayi). Stale entries (grace ke andar) nahi hatati.

`unref()` kyun: Node mein ek active timer process ko zinda rakhta hai. Agar ek CLI script ya test cache banaye aur timer ref'd ho, toh script kabhi exit nahi karegi -- 'process hang' bug. Code comment: 'a cache must never be the reason a process does not exit'. Test ise directly check karta hai: `setInterval` spy karke `timer.hasRef()` false.

`close()` timer ko `clearInterval` se rokta hai; do baar call karna safe hai; cache uske baad bhi kaam karta hai, bas lazy expiry ke saath. Sweep option na do toh koi timer banta hi nahi (test 'no sweepIntervalMs = no timer' `vi.getTimerCount()` 0 check karta hai). Invalid interval (0, -1, NaN, Infinity) `RangeError`.

Mutations S1 (unref nahi), S2 (close rokta nahi), S3 (sweep purge nahi karta) teeno pakde gaye.
why_needed: Lazy expiry se unread expired entries memory hold karti hain. Sweep woh memory free karta hai -- bina process ko zinda rakhe.
real_world_analogy: Society ka safai wala jo har hafte aata hai: tumhe uske aane ka wait nahi karna (tum khud bhi expired cheez phenk dete ho), aur agar society band ho rahi hai toh woh usse rokta nahi.
how_it_works: `setInterval` + `unref()`; `purgeExpired()` Map iterate karke delete karta hai (iteration ke dauran current key delete karna Map mein safe hai). `close()` timer clear karke `undefined` set karta hai.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts constructor ka sweep block, `purgeExpired()` aur `close()`. `test/ttl.test.ts` describe 'sweep timer': fake timers ke saath 'removes expired entries on its interval without any read', 'is unref'd: it never keeps the process alive', 'close() stops it, twice is fine, and the cache keeps working with lazy expiry', aur ek real timers wala test jo fixed time ki jagah 10 s tak sweep ka wait karta hai. README example `sweepIntervalMs: 30_000`.

Process exit ko block nahi karta
Optional: chahiye toh hi timer
disadvantages: purgeExpired O(n) hai, bade cache par ek tick mein poora walk
Interval ke beech `size` phir bhi expired entries count karta hai
common_mistakes: Timer ko unref na karna (scripts / tests hang)
close() bhool jaana jab cache short-lived object hai (timer callback cache ko reference karta hai, toh GC nahi hota)
Sweep ko correctness ke liye zaroori samajhna

question: What is the load context (ttlMs, refresh, isCurrent) passed to the loader, and what is each field for?
answer_hinglish:
Stage 2 ne loader ka doosra argument add kiya: `LoadContext`. Loader ka signature `(signal, context) => Promise<V> | V` hai -- purane loaders jo sirf `signal` lete the woh bina change chalte hain (backward compatible).

`ttlMs`: jis TTL ke saath loaded value store hogi (call ka `ttlMs`, warna cache default). Loader ISE BADAL sakta hai -- jaise HTTP response ke `max-age` se, ya TwoLevelCache mein Redis copy ke bache hue PTTL se. Invalid value (jaise -5) poore load ko `RangeError` se fail karta hai, har waiter ko; negative value phir bhi `negativeTtlMs` par cap hoti hai.

`refresh`: true jab yeh stale-while-revalidate ka background refresh hai (koi caller is par wait nahi kar raha). Loader isse alag logging ya lower priority de sakta hai.

`isCurrent()`: kya yeh load abhi bhi key ka current VERSION hai? Load shuru hone ke baad `delete`, `set` ya `clear` ne key ko chhua toh false. Implementation literally `() => this.flights.get(key) === flight` hai -- flight object hi version hai. Kyun chahiye: jo loader kahin AUR bhi likhta hai, use pata hona chahiye ki cache khud yeh value store nahi karega. TwoLevelCache `loadThrough` mein `if (context.isCurrent()) this.writeBehind(...)` karta hai, taaki purana DB row Redis mein na phail jaaye.

PLAN.md ka decision: Redis ko LruCache ke andar special-case karne ki jagah yeh teen generic hooks; 'TwoLevelCache is built on these three'.
why_needed: Loader ko kabhi value ki freshness pata hoti hai (max-age), aur kabhi use second store mein likhna hota hai. Context ke bina yeh sab LruCache ke andar hardcode karna padta.
real_world_analogy: Courier ko diya gaya job slip: 'delivery kab tak valid hai' (ttlMs, courier badal sakta hai agar sender ne kuch aur bola), 'urgent customer wait kar raha hai ya stock refill hai' (refresh), aur ek phone number jisse woh confirm kare ki order cancel to nahi hua (isCurrent).
how_it_works: `startLoad` context banata hai; loader resolve hone ke baad `if (this.flights.get(key) === flight)` tabhi `checkTtl(context.ttlMs)` aur store `loadedTtl(value, context.ttlMs)` ke saath.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts `LoadContext` interface aur `startLoad()`. `test/swr.test.ts` describe 'the load context': 'tells the loader the TTL it will get and whether it is a refresh' (seen `[{100,false},{7,false},{100,true}]`), 'a loader can set the TTL of the value it returns (e.g. from an HTTP max-age)', 'an invalid TTL set by the loader fails the load for every waiter', 'isCurrent() is true while the load is the key's version, false after delete / set'. src/two-level.ts `loadThrough` teeno use karta hai. Mutations C1-C4 sab pakde gaye.
advantages: Backward compatible (doosra argument)
Generic hooks: L2 bina LruCache badle
Stale writes doosre store mein bhi rukte hain
disadvantages: Mutable ttlMs field: loader galat value de sakta hai (isliye validate hota hai)
isCurrent() ek snapshot hai: check ke turant baad delete aa sakta hai
common_mistakes: isCurrent() check kiye bina external store mein likhna
Loader mein ttlMs ko 0 ya negative set karna
refresh ko 'caller wait kar raha hai' samajhna
follow_up_questions: Why is the flight object itself the version, instead of a counter?
Can isCurrent() be true at check time and the value still be stale in Redis?
How would you use ctx.ttlMs with an HTTP Cache-Control header?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Context ek mutable object hai -- simple, par loader ko trust karna padta hai; isliye load ke baad `checkTtl` validate karta hai. Alternative return type `{ value, ttlMs }` hota, jo har loader ka signature tod deta.
advanced.failure_scenarios: isCurrent() check aur Redis write ke beech window hai: check true, phir doosre replica ka set. Yeh window TwoLevelCache SET NX aur tombstones se band karta hai -- isCurrent() akela kaafi nahi.
advanced.alternatives: Loader ke return mein metadata, ya cache par per-key version counter (generation number) jise loader compare kare. Flight object identity zyada simple hai: koi counter overflow ya map nahi.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Context per load ek chhota object hai -- loads misses jitne hi hain, toh scale par negligible. Bade fan-out (ek load jo kai stores mein likhe) mein isCurrent() har write se pehle check karna padega.

question: Why did cache-kit choose a Map over the textbook doubly linked list + hash map for LRU, and what did that choice cost?
answer_hinglish:
Textbook LRU: ek hash map (key -> node) aur ek doubly linked list (recency order); hit par node unlink karke head par, evict tail se. Sab O(1). PLAN.md ne ise reject kiya: JavaScript `Map` already ek ordered hash map hai -- insertion order spec se guaranteed -- toh hit = `delete` + `set`, victim = pehli key. 'All O(1), no node objects, far less code ... the textbook answer ... here only adds code to get wrong.'

Faayde: pointer bugs ka koi chance nahi (prev / next update bhoolna classic LRU bug hai), har entry ke liye extra node object nahi, aur behaviour ek naive array model ke against 8 seeds x 3000 random steps mein verify hai.

Cost -- aur yeh interview mein honestly bolna chahiye -- engine internals ka asar dikha. Pehla version victim har eviction par naye `this.map.keys().next()` se nikaalta tha (README pehle `entries()` likhta tha; ek reviewer ne code comment aur guard test se compare karke theek karwaya). Benchmark ne 10 401.9 ns per evicting set dikhaya (10 000 entries, Windows 11, Ryzen 5 4500, Node 20.20.1) -- `Map.get` ka ~150x. Likely cause (README: V8 source nahi padha, sirf fix ka effect measure hua): deleted entries table mein holes chhodti hain, aur naya iterator slot 0 se shuru hokar har hole walk karta hai. Fix: ek long-lived iterator -> 548.8 / 664.6 ns (do runs, machine busy thi, toh orders of magnitude ki tarah padho). Linked list mein yeh problem hoti hi nahi. Matlab: built-in structure ne code bachaya, par uski performance guarantee runtime ke implementation par depend karti hai, aur usse benchmark se hi pakda.
why_needed: Data structure choice code size, bug surface aur performance teeno ko affect karta hai. Yahan simplicity jeeti, aur performance trap benchmark se pakda gaya.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ka almirah khud banane (linked list) vs readymade almirah lena (Map): readymade jaldi aur sahi lagta hai, par uske drawers ke andar ki rail kaise chalti hai woh tumhare control mein nahi -- ek drawer atak gaya toh pata tab chala jab roz kholne laga.
how_it_works: Map insertion order = recency. Victim = long-lived `keys()` iterator ka `next()`: spec ke hisaab se iterator deleted entries skip karta hai aur baad mein append hui entries visit karta hai, toh `next()` hamesha LRU key hai.
in_this_project: PLAN.md 'LRU on a JavaScript Map, not a hand-written doubly linked list'. src/cache.ts `private oldest: Iterator<K> = this.map.keys()` aur `evictOldest()` ka lamba comment. README 'Overhead': before-fix raw `bench/reference-results/2026-11-23-win32-before-iterator-fix.json`. `test/lru.test.ts` 'evictions reuse one Map iterator': 1000 evictions mein `Map.prototype.keys` max 1 baar.
advantages: Bahut kam code, pointer bugs nahi
Koi per-entry node object nahi
Order spec se guaranteed aur model test se verified
disadvantages: Performance engine internals par depend (deleted slot holes)
Hit = do hash operations (delete + set)
O(1) 'amortized' hai, strict nahi
common_mistakes: Map.keys().next() har eviction par (holes walk karta hai)
Bina benchmark ke 'Map O(1) hai' maan lena
Linked list banana aur prev/next ek jagah update bhoolna
follow_up_questions: Explain why a fresh iterator walks over holes and a long-lived one does not.
How was the fix protected against regression without a timing assertion?
When would you still write the linked list?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Simplicity aur correctness (Map) vs predictable performance (khud ka linked list). Map choose karke code chhota hua; performance ka ek trap mila jo long-lived iterator se fix hua.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Long-lived iterator ki invariant toot jaaye (koi key iterator ke position se PEHLE insert ho) toh galat victim nikal sakta hai. Spec ke hisaab se aisa nahi hota kyunki keys sirf end par append hoti hain; `clear()` iterator reset karta hai (L6 equivalent mutant).
advanced.alternatives: Doubly linked list + Map<K, Node>; ya array-based layout (index arrays + key -> index map, jo kuch established libraries karti hain; is repo mein compare nahi kiya gaya). Dono zyada code, par engine-independent.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x entries par O(n) cheezein (purgeExpired, keys()) costly; hit path O(1) rehta hai. Bahut bade caches par per-entry object overhead dominate karega -- tab typed-array layout socha ja sakta hai. Memory per entry measure nahi hua (README).
advanced.production_improvements: Bench ko CI mein track karna (absolute timing nahi, relative to Map.get floor); Linux par bhi measure karna (README: not measured); memory per entry measure karna.

question: Why does cache-kit default its clock to performance.now() instead of Date.now(), and why is it injectable?
answer_hinglish:
TTL ka calculation `expiresAt = now() + ttl` hai, toh clock agar jump kare toh expiry bhi jump karegi. `Date.now()` wall clock hai -- NTP sync, admin ka manual change, ya VM / laptop suspend se resume hone par woh aage ya peeche koodh sakta hai. Agar wall clock 1 ghanta aage gaya toh cache ki HAR entry ek saath expire -- poora cache ek saath cold, aur saare misses DB par (ek self-made stampede). Peeche gaya toh entries apne TTL se zyada jeeti hain -- purana data 'resurrect'.

`performance.now()` monotonic hai: sirf aage badhta hai, process start se relative, wall clock changes se independent. Duration measure karne ke liye yahi sahi tool hai. Code: `this.now = options.now ?? (() => performance.now())`, aur option comment: 'monotonic: a wall-clock jump cannot expire everything'.

Injectable kyun: tests real time ka wait nahi karte. `test/support.ts` ka `manualClock()` ek object hai jiska `now()` ek number return karta hai aur `advance(ms)` usse badhata hai. Isse boundary tests exact hote hain -- 'live at 99, expired AT 100' -- bina sleep, bina flakiness. Sirf ek sweep test real timers use karta hai, woh bhi fixed time ki jagah 10 s tak event ka wait karta hai.

Catch: monotonic time process-local hai, do machines ke beech compare nahi ho sakta. Isliye TwoLevelCache Redis mein absolute timestamp nahi, relative TTL (PX) aur PTTL bhejta hai.
why_needed: Cache ki expiry duration par based hai; wall clock jump karne par mass expiry ya stale data resurrect ho sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Stopwatch vs deewar ki ghadi: race time naapne ke liye stopwatch use karte ho, kyunki deewar ki ghadi ko koi bhi beech mein aage-peeche kar sakta hai.
how_it_works: Har expiry decision `this.now()` se. Default monotonic, option `now` test hook. Entries mein relative-to-process times store hote hain.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts `LruCacheOptions.now` aur constructor. `test/support.ts` `manualClock(start = 1000)`. Lagbhag har TTL / SWR / negative test `now: clock.now` pass karta hai. README options table: '`now` | `performance.now` | test hook; monotonic so a wall-clock jump does not expire everything'.
advantages: Wall clock jump se mass expiry nahi
Tests deterministic aur fast
Boundary exact test ho sakti hai
disadvantages: Monotonic time machines ke beech share nahi ho sakta
Fake timers aur injected clock alag cheezein hain: sweep test ko dono chahiye
common_mistakes: Date.now() se TTL calculate karna
Tests mein sleep karke TTL check karna (flaky)
Monotonic timestamp ko Redis / doosri machine bhejna

question: Why does cache-kit refuse to cache loader errors, even with negative caching on? What does that cost during an outage?
answer_hinglish:
Rule: loader ka error KABHI cache nahi hota. Single flight mein jitne callers wait kar rahe the sabko wahi error milta hai, flight detach hoti hai, aur AGLA call phir se load karta hai. Negative caching on ho tab bhi -- `negative.test.ts` mein 'errors are still NOT cached' test hai.

Kyun: loader error usually transient hota hai -- timeout, connection reset, DB restart, deploy. README ka argument: error cache karoge toh 50 ms ka blip us key ke liye poore error-TTL ka outage ban jaata hai. Agar error TTL 5 s hai aur DB 50 ms ke liye hichki le, toh hot key 5 s tak sab users ke liye fail. 'Not found' alag hai: woh ek valid answer hai, isliye woh short negative TTL ke saath cache hota hai. Jis loader ko pata hai ki error ka matlab 404 hai, woh `null` return kare.

Cost (README 'Known', honestly likha): jis key ka load hamesha fail hota hai, uska HAR miss loader tak jaata hai -- per key ek waqt mein ek load (concurrent callers phir bhi coalesce hote hain), par sequential traffic ke liye koi protection nahi. DB down hai toh cache use bachata nahi. SWR ke case mein: failed refresh stale value rakhta hai aur agli stale read bina backoff ke phir try karti hai -- hot key DB par back-to-back ek refresh bhejti rehti hai jab tak grace khatam na ho.

Senior answer: error caching cache ka kaam nahi; overload protection ke liye circuit breaker / timeout (projects/18-resilience) loader ke andar lagao. Opt-in error caching aur refresh backoff dono 'NOT implemented' list mein hain.

Par agar dukaan sach mein band hai, toh har customer ko khud jaake dekhna padega; uske liye mall ka guard (circuit breaker) better hai jo sabko bata de.

question: Why do get, peek and has never return a stale entry, even though getOrLoad does?
answer_hinglish:
Stage 2 decision: stale entry (TTL ke baad, grace ke andar) `get` / `peek` / `has` ke liye ABSENT hai -- `get` miss count karta hai, `has` false deta hai -- par entry delete nahi hoti, `getOrLoad` ke liye map mein rehti hai.

Reasoning (PLAN.md aur `get` ka comment): stale-while-revalidate ka contract hai 'purana do AUR refresh karo'. `get` ke paas loader nahi hai, toh woh refresh shuru hi nahi kar sakta. Agar `get` stale return karta, toh jo callers `getOrLoad` use nahi karte unke liye entry grace khatam hone tak purani rehti, koi refresh nahi -- matlab `ttlMs` ka matlab hi khatam, effective TTL ban jaata `ttlMs + staleMs`. Stale data ek conscious choice hai jo sirf woh caller kare jo refresh bhi trigger kar sake.

Consistency details: `delete(key)` wahi return karta hai jo `has` deta -- stale entry ke liye false -- par entry hata deta hai (test 'delete of a stale entry returns false (like has) and removes it'). `size` stale entries count karta hai. `purgeExpired` / sweep sirf grace ke baad wali entries hatate hain. Eviction mein stale victim ko limit ka reason milta hai.

Alternative: `get` stale de aur ek flag bhi (`{ value, stale: true }`) -- par API badalta aur har caller ko flag handle karna padta. Mutations R2 (get / peek / has fresh AT expiresAt), R4 (`get` stale return kare) aur R15 (delete stale par true) pakde gaye.
why_needed: TTL ek contract hai. Agar ek API stale data chupchaap de bina refresh kiye, toh woh contract tootta hai.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant ka buffet: kal ka khana 'staff ke liye' rakha hai jab tak naya ban raha hai (getOrLoad) -- par customer ke menu (get) par woh 'available' nahi dikhaya jaata, kyunki customer ke paas naya banwane ka option nahi.
how_it_works: `get` / `peek` / `has` private `fresh()` use karte hain: `live()` + `now < expiresAt`. `getOrLoad` `live()` use karta hai jo stale bhi deta hai.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts `get` ka comment: 'A stale entry ... is NOT returned: get has no loader, so it cannot refresh it, and returning it would make the TTL mean nothing to every caller that does not use getOrLoad.' `fresh()` vs `live()`. `test/swr.test.ts` 'get / peek / has do NOT return a stale entry (get counts a miss), but keep it for getOrLoad'. TwoLevelCache bhi isi rule par: L1 stale grace per replica hai, Redis sirf fresh TTL rakhta hai (PLAN).

Stale sirf wahan jahan refresh guaranteed
Simple API, koi flag nahi
disadvantages: get-only callers ko grace ka faayda nahi milta

question: Lazy expiry with an optional sweep vs a timer per entry vs an always-on sweep -- and why does the TTL count from set instead of sliding on reads?
answer_hinglish:
Expiry ke teen designs. (1) Har entry ka apna `setTimeout`: lakhon entries = lakhon timers, har set / replace par timer cancel + naya, aur timers process ko zinda rakhte hain. (2) Hamesha chalne wala sweep: correctness ke liye zaroori nahi, aur O(n) walk har interval. (3) cache-kit ka choice: LAZY expiry correctness deta hai -- `get`, `peek`, `has`, `delete`, `getOrLoad` sab expiry check karte hain, expired value kabhi return nahi hoti, zero timers. Memory reclaim ke liye OPTIONAL `sweepIntervalMs`, unref'd, `close()` se band. PLAN: correctness aur memory alag concerns.

Lazy ka cost honestly: `size` expired entries count karta hai jab tak koi chhoo na le; unread expired entries memory leti hain (bounded phir bhi -- maxEntries / maxWeight). Eviction victim agar expired tha toh `expired` report hota hai, toh metrics sahi rehte hain.

TTL `set` se, sliding nahi: PLAN.md -- 'A hot key must still be refreshed now and then, or it would never pick up changes.' Sliding expiry mein har read TTL badhata hai; jo key har second padhi jaati hai woh KABHI expire nahi hogi, toh DB mein badla hua data kabhi nahi dikhega. Absolute TTL staleness ka upper bound guarantee karta hai. Test 'get does not extend the TTL (expiry counts from set)' yeh lock karta hai.

Sliding expiry, refresh-ahead, aur LFU sab 'NOT implemented' hain. Senior framing: TTL = 'max staleness budget'; idle memory ke liye LRU + sweep already hai, toh sliding ka faayda chhota aur risk bada.
why_needed: Expiry design memory, CPU, process lifecycle aur data freshness guarantee chaaron ko affect karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Sabzi wale ki do policies: har tamatar par alag alarm lagana (timer per entry), roz shaam poora thela chhaanna (sweep), ya bechte waqt dekh lena aur kabhi kabhi saaf karna (lazy + optional sweep). Aur 'jo tamatar log zyada uthate hain uski expiry badha do' (sliding) -- matlab popular tamatar kabhi phenka hi nahi jaayega, chahe sad jaaye.
how_it_works: `expiresAt = now + ttl` sirf `store()` mein set hota hai; `hit()` / `touch()` expiresAt nahi chhoote. Lazy check `live()` mein. Sweep = `setInterval(purgeExpired)` + `unref()`.
in_this_project: PLAN.md decisions 'Lazy expiry, plus an OPTIONAL sweep' aur 'TTL counts from set, not from the last read (no sliding expiry)'. src/cache.ts `store()`, `live()`, constructor sweep block. `test/ttl.test.ts` 'get does not extend the TTL', 'set again restarts the TTL', aur sweep tests. README 'Known': '`size` includes expired entries until something touches them or the sweep runs'.

Expired value kabhi return nahi
Absolute TTL = staleness ka guaranteed upper bound
Sweep optional aur process-safe
disadvantages: Unread expired entries memory lete hain
size misleading ho sakta hai
Hot key bhi TTL par reload hoti hai (SWR uska latency cost chhupata hai)
common_mistakes: Sliding expiry se 'hit ratio badhega' sochna aur stale data bhool jaana
Har entry par setTimeout
Sweep ko correctness mechanism samajhna
follow_up_questions: When is sliding expiry actually the right choice (sessions)?

advanced.failure_scenarios: Sweep band aur traffic pattern aisa ki keys ek baar likhi jaayein aur kabhi na padhi jaayein: memory maxEntries tak bharti hai expired entries se -- bounded, par wasted. Sliding expiry hoti toh config cache jaisi hot key DB badalne ke baad bhi purani rehti.
advanced.alternatives: Redis jaisa hybrid (lazy + random sampling active expiry); Caffeine ka hierarchical timing wheel (O(1) expiry); sliding expiry with absolute max lifetime (sessions ke liye).

question: Walk through weighOf(): why must weigh() return an integer, and how does set() stay unchanged when it throws?
answer_hinglish:
`weighOf()` user ka `weigh(value, key)` call karta hai aur result validate karta hai: `if (!Number.isSafeInteger(w) || w < 0) throw new RangeError(...)`. Matlab -1, NaN, Infinity, 1.5, 0.1, string '3', undefined, null -- sab reject. 0 valid hai (empty string 0 bytes).

Fractions kyun reject? Total weight ek running sum hai: har store par `+= weight`, har remove par `-= weight`. Floating point mein yeh drift karta hai -- README ka example: `0.1 + 0.2 - 0.1 - 0.2` 0 nahi, `2.8e-17` hai. Lakhon set / remove ke baad total entries se match nahi karega, aur weight eviction galat decisions lega. Bytes waise bhi integers hain. Yeh rule mutation testing se aaya: mutation W5 (remove weight subtract na kare) ne weight-eviction loop ko infinite bana diya aur test run hang ho gaya; uske baad do changes hue -- `size > 1` guard aur integer-only weights (naya mutation W7).

'Cache unchanged' kaise: `set()` ka order dekho -- pehle `checkTtl`, `checkStale`, phir `weighOf`, aur sirf UNKE BAAD `this.flights.delete(key)` aur `store()`. Throw kahin bhi ho, koi state touch nahi hui: purani value, total weight, running load sab waise ke waise. Test har bad value ke baad `peek("k")` 'old' aur `totalWeight` 1 check karta hai. Loaded value ke case mein weigh fail ho toh har waiter reject hota hai aur `loadErrors` +1.
why_needed: Galat weight silently total ko corrupt karta hai aur eviction galat karta hai. Loud failure bug ko turant dikhata hai; validate-before-mutate cache ko consistent rakhta hai.
real_world_analogy: Bank cashier pehle note check karta hai (nakli to nahi), PHIR drawer mein daalta hai. Agar drawer mein daal ke baad check karta, toh nakli note mila toh hisaab bigad chuka hota.
how_it_works: Validate (ttl, stale, weight) -> detach running load -> store. Weight integer hone se running total exact rehta hai.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts `weighOf()` aur `set()`. `test/lru.test.ts` 'weigh returning an invalid value throws RangeError and leaves the cache unchanged' (`[-1, NaN, Infinity, 1.5, 0.1, "3", undefined, null]`). `test/load.test.ts` 'weigh returning an invalid value for a loaded value rejects every waiter and caches nothing'. README Mutation section: W4 (invalid accepted), W7 (fractions accepted, 1 test ne pakda).

Bug turant RangeError se dikhta hai
Fail hone par cache consistent

question: Explain evictOldest() and its long-lived iterator: what was slow before, what were the measured numbers, and how is the fix tested?
answer_hinglish:
Pehla version victim aise nikaalta tha: `this.map.keys().next()` -- har eviction par ek NAYA iterator. (README pehle `entries()` kehta tha; reviewer ne code comment, PLAN aur guard test -- jo `Map.prototype.keys` spy karta hai -- se compare karke correct karwaya.) Benchmark (`bench/overhead.mjs`, 10 000 entries, 1 000 000 ops per round, 200 000 warm-up, 7 rounds ka median) ne dikhaya: evicting set 10 401.9 ns per op, jabki us run mein `Map.get` 69.3 ns tha. README ka likely cause (V8 source nahi padha, sirf fix ka effect measure hua): delete ki hui entry Map ke table mein hole chhodti hai jab tak rehash na ho, aur naya iterator slot 0 se shuru hota hai -- toh har eviction pichhli saari evictions ke holes walk karti thi.

Fix: class mein ek field `private oldest: Iterator<K> = this.map.keys()`, aur har eviction `this.oldest.next()`. Spec ke hisaab se Map iterator deleted entries skip karta hai aur baad mein append hui entries VISIT karta hai. Har live key iterator ki position par ya uske baad hai (keys sirf nikalti hain, ya hit / set par end mein re-append hoti hain), toh `next()` hamesha LRU key hai, aur har hole total mein ek hi baar walk hota hai. After: 548.8 ns (run 1) aur 664.6 ns (run 2), Windows 11, Ryzen 5 4500, Node 20.20.1 -- machine busy thi (Map floor 36.9 se 78.9 tak hila), toh orders of magnitude ki tarah padho.

Edge: finished iterator hamesha finished rehta hai, toh `done` par naya iterator (README: unreachable, mutant L7 equivalent). `clear()` bhi iterator reset karta hai (L6 equivalent). Testing: purana code wapas daalne par (L8) pehle KOI test fail nahi hua -- pure performance change. Ab test `Map.prototype.keys` ko spy karke 1000 evictions mein max 1 call assert karta hai -- timing assertion ke bina, kyunki timing tests is machine par flaky the.
why_needed: Ek O(1) claim ko benchmark ne galat pakda. Fix aur uska regression test dikhata hai ki performance bugs ko bhi bina flaky timing ke test kiya ja sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Register mein kate hue naam: har baar page 1 se padhna shuru karo toh saare kate naam phir se padhne padte hain. Ek bookmark rakh lo jahan tak pahunche the -- har kata naam sirf ek baar paar karna padega.
how_it_works: `next()` -> done ho toh naya iterator. `key = next.value`, entry nikaal ke `evict(key, deadAt check ? expired : reason)`. Iterator invariant: sab live keys uski position ke baad.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts `evictOldest()` ka comment numbers aur raw file ka naam deta hai. Raw: `bench/reference-results/2026-11-23-win32-before-iterator-fix.json` (10401.9), `-run1.json` (548.8), `-run2.json` (664.6). `test/lru.test.ts` 'evictions reuse one Map iterator instead of creating one per eviction' -- beech mein `c.get(i - 50)` bhi karta hai taaki beech mein holes banein.
advantages: Evicting set ~10.4 us se ~0.55-0.66 us (is machine par)
LRU order unchanged (model test pass)
Regression test bina timing ke
disadvantages: Iterator invariant ko samajhna padta hai
Engine-specific behaviour par based diagnosis (V8 source verify nahi hua)
common_mistakes: Performance ko timing assertion se test karna (flaky)
Har eviction par `map.keys().next()`
Iterator invariant todne wala change (jaise key ko beech mein insert)

question: Walk through emit() in events.ts: why is a throwing event handler ignored, and which events exist?
answer_hinglish:
`emit(handler, event)` chhota function hai: handler nahi hai toh return; warna `try { handler(event) } catch { /* ignored on purpose */ }`. Comment reason deta hai: 'telemetry must never change what the caller gets'.

Socho bina try/catch ke kya hota: `onEvent` mein logger ek undefined field padh ke throw karta hai. Event `store()` ke andar emit hota hai -- eviction ke beech. Exception `set()` se bahar aata: caller ko error milta jabki value shayad store ho chuki thi, aur eviction loop aadha chhoot jaata (limit violate). `startLoad` mein `load` event throw karta toh load ka promise reject, sab waiters fail -- sirf ek logging bug ki wajah se. Metrics / logging ko kabhi core behaviour nahi todna chahiye.

Events (`CacheEvent<K>` union): `evict` (key, reason size / weight / expired), `reject` (key, weight), `load`, `load-error` (error), `refresh`, `refresh-error`, `load-abort`. Hits / misses events nahi hain -- woh har call par hote hain, counters mein hain. Ek handler sab feed kar sakta hai -- file comment ka example: `metrics.inc(`cache_${e.type}`, ...)`.

Test 'a throwing handler is ignored everywhere and changes nothing': handler har baar throw karta hai, ek scripted run 8 emits karta hai (load, evict size, evict expired, reject, load + load-error, load + load-abort) aur har call ka return value normal rehta hai, `calls` 8. Mutation E1 (handler contain na ho) pakda gaya. TwoLevelCache ka apna `emit` bhi same pattern follow karta hai.
why_needed: Observability code bhi buggy hota hai. Agar woh cache ke result ko badal sake, toh ek logger ka bug production outage ban jaata hai.

question: Walk through store(): the order of operations, the two eviction loops, and why the weight loop has a size > 1 guard.
answer_hinglish:
`store(key, value, weight, ttl, stale, negative)` har write ka common path hai (`set` aur successful load dono). Order:

1. `this.remove(key)` -- purani entry (agar hai) map se aur uska weight total se nikalo. Yeh eviction nahi, koi event nahi.
2. Too-heavy check: `weight > maxWeight` -> `rejected++`, `reject` event, `return false`. Purani value step 1 mein already gayi -- jaan-boojh kar.
3. `expiresAt = ttl === undefined ? Infinity : now() + ttl`; entry set `{ value, weight, expiresAt, deadAt: expiresAt + stale, negative }`; naya key Map ke END par (most recent).
4. `weightTotal += weight`.
5. `while (map.size > maxEntries) evictOldest("size")`.
6. `while (weightTotal > maxWeight && map.size > 1) evictOldest("weight")`.

`size > 1` guard ki kahani: mutation W5 (remove weight subtract na kare) ne total ko entries se zyada bana diya; loop ne sab evict kar diya aur phir bhi total limit se upar -- khaali map par infinite loop. Vitest run kabhi khatam nahi hua, runner ka 300 s timeout sirf shell maar paaya, 12 orphan node processes spin karte rahe. Ab loop tab bhi rukta hai jab sirf naya entry bacha. Sahi bookkeeping mein yeh no-op hai -- naya entry khud `<= maxWeight` hai (step 2 ne guarantee kiya) aur last mein hai -- isliye W8 (guard hatao) equivalent mutant hai. Guard ka faayda: bookkeeping bug ab hung process nahi, galat evictions deta hai jo tests dekh sakte hain.

Naya entry hamesha last mein hai, toh LRU loop kabhi usse victim nahi banata (jab tak woh akela na ho).
why_needed: Write path par order of operations hi invariants (weight total, limits, recency) ko sahi rakhta hai. Defensive guard ek bug ko hang ki jagah visible failure banata hai.
real_world_analogy: Parking mein nayi gaadi: pehle wahi purani gaadi ki jagah khaali karo, check karo gaadi parking mein fit hoti bhi hai, phir park karo, phir agar jagah zyada ho gayi toh sabse purani gaadiyon ko tow karo -- par nayi gaadi ko kabhi nahi.
how_it_works: Map append = most recent. Size loop pehle, weight loop baad mein, dono same LRU iterator se. Har victim ka reason `evictOldest` mein deadAt se decide.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts `store()` aur uske comment: 'The new entry is last and weighs <= maxWeight on its own, so with correct bookkeeping this loop stops before reaching it. `size > 1` is a guard, not a rule'. README 'Found by a mutation: W5 hung the test run'. Model test har step ke baad `cache.totalWeight` ko model ke sum se compare karta hai.
advantages: Ek hi write path: set aur load same rules

question: Exercise: add an opt-in slidingExpiry option to LruCache so that a hit restarts the entry's TTL. Write the change and a vitest test.
answer_hinglish:
Pehle clear kar doon: sliding expiry is repo mein implement NAHI hai -- README 'NOT implemented' mein 'Sliding expiry (TTL refreshed on read)' listed hai, aur PLAN.md ne jaan-boojh kar absolute TTL choose kiya ('a hot key must still be refreshed now and then'). Toh yeh exercise opt-in feature ki tarah likhunga, default behaviour bilkul same.

Approach: (1) `LruCacheOptions` mein `slidingExpiry?: boolean`. (2) `Entry` ko yaad rakhna padega ki woh kis TTL aur grace ke saath store hui thi -- abhi sirf `expiresAt` / `deadAt` hai, toh `ttl` aur `stale` fields add. `store()` unhe bharega. (3) Restart kahan? Private `hit()` mein -- yeh `get` aur `getOrLoad` ke fresh hit dono ka common path hai. `peek` / `has` `hit()` call nahi karte, toh woh TTL nahi badhayenge (inspection side-effect free rehna chahiye). Stale hit bhi `hit()` nahi bulata -- stale entry refresh se nayi hogi, sliding se nahi.

Teen design decisions jo interview mein bolne chahiye: negatives KABHI slide nahi karte -- warna ek bot jo missing id baar baar maare, 'not found' ko hamesha zinda rakhega aur user create hone ke baad bhi 404 dikhega. Grace TTL ke saath move karti hai (`deadAt = expiresAt + stale`). Aur sliding ka asli risk: hot key kabhi expire nahi hogi, toh production mein iske saath ek absolute max-age cap bhi chahiye (follow-up). Tests manual clock se boundaries check karte hain; maine yeh chaaron tests ek patched copy par chala ke pass dekhe hain.
why_needed: Session-type data (idle hone par hi hatna chahiye) ke liye sliding expiry common requirement hai; exercise dikhata hai ki entry metadata aur hit path kaise extend karte hain bina default behaviour tode.
real_world_analogy: Gym membership jo har visit par ek mahina aage badh jaati hai: regular aane wale ki kabhi expire nahi hoti -- isliye gym ek 'max 1 saal phir renewal' rule bhi rakhta hai.
how_it_works: Hit par `expiresAt = now + entry.ttl`, `deadAt = expiresAt + entry.stale`, phir `touch()`. Sirf jab option on, ttl defined (Infinity bhi defined hai, uska restart Infinity hi rahega) aur entry negative nahi.
in_this_project: Real code jahan change jaayega: src/cache.ts `Entry<V>` interface, `store()` ki `this.map.set(...)` line, aur private `hit()`. Existing test `test/ttl.test.ts` 'get does not extend the TTL (expiry counts from set)' default behaviour lock karta hai -- option off hone par woh pass hona chahiye. Test helper `manualClock` `test/support.ts` se.
advantages: Opt-in: default behaviour aur saare existing tests same
Idle keys naturally expire, active keys bachti hain
Change chhota: ek option, do fields, ek branch
disadvantages: Hot key kabhi refresh nahi hogi -- stale data ka risk (PLAN ka reason)
Har entry par do extra fields (memory)
Model test ko bhi update karna padega agar option model mein jaaye
common_mistakes: peek / has se bhi TTL badhana
Negative entries ko bhi slide karna
deadAt update bhool jaana (grace purani position par atki rahegi)
Absolute max-age cap na rakhna
follow_up_questions: How would you add an absolute maxAgeMs cap on top of sliding expiry?
Should a stale hit via getOrLoad also slide? Why or why not?
How would you extend the randomized model test for this option?

question: Exercise: protect the LRU from one-time scans with an LFU-ish admission counter (a key is cached only after N recent requests). Write it on top of LruCache with a vitest test.
answer_hinglish:
Problem: LRU har nayi key ko admit karta hai. Ek report ya crawler 10 000 alag ids ek ek baar padhe, toh har id cache mein aati hai aur hot keys bahar -- hit ratio gir jaata hai, jabki scan wali keys dobara kabhi nahi padhi jaayengi. Is repo mein LFU / W-TinyLFU admission implement NAHI hai (README 'NOT implemented', PLAN 'Not in scope': 'what Caffeine does'), toh yeh exercise ek simple version hai.

Design: LruCache ko chhede bina ek wrapper. `FrequencyAdmission` har request par key ka count badhata hai; har `sampleSize` requests par saare counts aadhe (aging -- TinyLFU ke reset ka idea), aur 0 hone wale counts delete -- isse counter map bounded rehta hai aur purani popularity fade hoti hai. `AdmittingCache.getOrLoad`: count `>= minHits` ho ya key pehle se cache mein ho toh normal `cache.getOrLoad` (single flight, TTL, stats sab wahi). Warna loader seedha chalao, store mat karo.

Do subtle points. Pehla: bypass path par bhi single flight chahiye, warna 100 concurrent requests ek naye key ke liye 100 loader calls -- stampede wapas. Isliye ek chhota `bypass` Map of promises. Doosra: `Loader` signature ko context chahiye; maine `isCurrent: () => false` diya -- cache.ts mein iska matlab hi hai 'yeh value store nahi hogi', toh jo loader doosre store (jaise Redis) mein likhta hai woh bhi nahi likhega.

Limitation honestly: bypass load ka signal kabhi abort nahi hota (caller signal support nahi kiya), aur yeh sirf 'doorkeeper' hai -- real W-TinyLFU candidate ki frequency ko victim ki frequency se compare karta hai, jiske liye LRU victim tak access chahiye. Tests ek patched-free copy par chala ke pass dekhe hain.
why_needed: Scan resistance real production problem hai (batch jobs, crawlers). Admission policy bina eviction policy badle cache pollution rokti hai.
real_world_analogy: Club ka bouncer: pehli baar aaye log ko andar ki VIP table nahi milti, bar se drink le ke jaa sakte hain; jo hafte mein do baar aaye use table milti hai. Aur har mahine register ke count aadhe -- purane regulars bhi dheere dheere 'naye' ho jaate hain.
how_it_works: record(key) -> count. Admit agar count >= minHits ya cache.has(key). Na ho toh bypass Map se single-flight loader call, value return, store nahi. Aging: har sampleSize par counts >> 1.
in_this_project: Real pieces jo wrapper use karta hai: `LruCache.getOrLoad`, `LruCache.has`, aur `Loader` / `LoadContext` types src/cache.ts se. `isCurrent()` ka meaning src/cache.ts `LoadContext` comment mein: 'so it does not spread a value the cache itself will not store'. Model ke liye compare: existing `test/load.test.ts` '100 concurrent getOrLoad for one key -> the loader runs ONCE' wahi property admitted keys ke liye deta hai.
advantages: Scan / one-hit wonders hot keys ko nahi nikaalte
LruCache unchanged, wrapper opt-in
Counter map aging se bounded
Bypass path par bhi single flight
disadvantages: Pehli request(s) hamesha loader tak (admission ka cost)
Counter map extra memory (sampleSize tak keys)
Victim-vs-candidate comparison nahi, sirf threshold
Bypass load abort nahi hota
common_mistakes: Bypass path par single flight bhool jaana
Counts kabhi aage na karna (unbounded map, stale popularity)
Admitted key ka stale entry has() false deta hai -- yaad rakhna ki wrapper count se admit karega
follow_up_questions: How does W-TinyLFU use a Count-Min Sketch instead of a Map of counters?
How would you compare the candidate's frequency with the LRU victim's?
How would you measure that admission actually improved the hit ratio?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Wrapper approach LruCache ko untouched rakhta hai par victim tak access nahi deta, isliye sirf threshold admission possible hai; asli TinyLFU ke liye eviction path ke andar hook chahiye.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Burst traffic jahan har key sach mein do baar aati hai (jaise ek retry) -- sab admit ho jaayengi, filter kaam nahi karega. minHits bada rakha toh naye hot keys late admit hote hain (cold start penalty). Counter map sampleSize tak keys hold karta hai.
advanced.alternatives: Count-Min Sketch (fixed memory, approximate counts) + doorkeeper Bloom filter (W-TinyLFU / Caffeine); ARC / 2Q (recency + frequency queues); ya scan wale callers ko bypass flag dena.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x-100x distinct keys par Map of counters memory mein bhaari -- sketch (kuch KB fixed) chahiye. Aging ka O(n) walk har sampleSize par spike deta hai; sketch mein halving bhi O(width) hai par fixed.
advanced.production_improvements: Hit ratio A/B measure karna (admission on/off); sketch-based counter; admit decision ko victim ki frequency se compare karna; bypass loads ke liye caller signal support.

question: During a database outage, what exactly does a hot key do under stale-while-revalidate in cache-kit, and how would you add refresh backoff?
answer_hinglish:
Scenario: key `config:pricing`, `ttlMs` 30 s, `staleMs` 60 s, hazaaron reads/sec, aur DB down ho gaya. Code ke hisaab se exactly yeh hota hai.

TTL khatam hote hi pehli `getOrLoad` stale value turant deti hai aur ek refresh shuru karti hai. Jab tak woh refresh chal raha hai, baaki stale reads `this.flights.has(key)` dekh ke naya refresh NAHI shuru karte -- ek waqt mein ek. Refresh fail hua: `refresh-error` event, `refreshErrors` +1 (aur `loadErrors` +1), entry waise hi rehti hai. Agli stale read turant naya refresh shuru karti hai -- koi backoff nahi. Matlab DB par us key ke liye back-to-back ek refresh, jab tak grace khatam na ho. README 'Known' yahi likhta hai. Users ko grace bhar purana data milta hai -- yahi grace ka purpose hai.

Grace khatam (`deadAt`): entry `expired` ke saath remove, ab normal miss -- callers loader ka wait karte hain aur error paate hain (error cache nahi hota). Concurrent misses coalesce hote hain, toh per key ek load at a time.

Aur bura case: agar loader kabhi settle hi na ho aur signal ignore kare, toh refresh flight hamesha ke liye atki -- naya refresh kabhi start nahi hoga, aur grace ke baad har caller usi stuck refresh mein join karega. Refresh cache ko permanent waiter maanta hai, toh caller abort usse abort nahi karta. Fix: loader mein timeout (projects/18-resilience ka TimeoutPolicy).

Backoff (NOT implemented) kaise add karunga: per key `nextRefreshAt` -- failed refresh par `now + min(base * 2^failures, cap)` with jitter; stale read sirf tab refresh shuru kare jab `now >= nextRefreshAt`; success par reset.
why_needed: Outage mein cache ka behaviour hi decide karta hai ki users ko kya dikhega aur recovering DB par kitna load aayega.
real_world_analogy: Pani ki tanki: municipal supply band hai, toh tanki ka pura pani (stale) chalta rehta hai. Par har 2 second mein koi motor on karke check kare ki supply aayi ya nahi -- motor jal jaayegi. Thoda ruk ruk ke check karna (backoff) samajhdari hai.
how_it_works: Stale path: `if (!this.flights.has(key)) this.startLoad(key, loader, options, true)`. Refresh flight `waiters: 1` se start (cache khud). Catch mein flight detach, entry untouched.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts `getOrLoad` stale branch aur `startLoad` (refresh ke liye `waiters: refresh ? 1 : 0`). `test/swr.test.ts` 'keeps serving the stale value until the grace ends, reports refresh-error, and the next stale read retries' (failing loader 2 baar call, grace ke baad `rejects.toBe(boom)`) aur 'a caller that joins the refresh and aborts does NOT abort the refresh'. README 'Known': no backoff; stuck loader. Mutation R11 (failed refresh stale entry drop kare) pakda gaya.
advantages: Users grace bhar purana data paate hain, errors nahi
Ek waqt mein per key ek hi refresh
Recovery fast: DB wapas aate hi agla refresh success
disadvantages: Back-to-back refreshes recovering DB par load
Stuck loader key ko hamesha ke liye atka sakta hai
Grace ke baad sab users ko error
common_mistakes: Loader mein timeout na lagana
staleMs ko outage ka plan samajhna bina monitoring ke
Backoff state ko delete / set par reset na karna
follow_up_questions: Why does a refresh count the cache as a permanent waiter?
What happens to the backoff map's memory with many keys?
Would you serve stale beyond the grace during an outage? What are the risks?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Simplicity (koi backoff state nahi) vs recovering backend ki protection. PLAN ne backoff 'more state' bol ke chhoda; ek hot key ke liye ek-at-a-time refresh already bounded hai, par bahut saari stale keys milke DB par steady load bana sakti hain.
advanced.failure_scenarios: DB slow (down nahi): refresh 5 s leta hai, us dauraan stale serve; theek. DB hang aur loader bina timeout: refresh kabhi settle nahi, grace ke baad sab callers stuck refresh par join, bina signal wale callers hamesha wait. DB flapping: har up-window mein saari stale keys ek saath refresh -- herd.
advanced.alternatives: Per-key exponential backoff with jitter; global circuit breaker jo open hone par refresh skip kare; 'serve stale on error' grace extension (`staleIfError`); refresh-ahead jo TTL se pehle hi refresh kare (NOT implemented).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x keys = 10x concurrent refreshes during outage (per key ek). 100x par yeh DB connection pool bhar dega -- global concurrency limit for refreshes (semaphore) ya breaker chahiye.
advanced.production_improvements: Loader ko timeout + breaker mein wrap karna; refreshErrors rate par alert; backoff state ka size bound; dashboards par staleHits vs hits outage detect karne ke liye.

question: How does cache-kit guarantee that a background refresh never overwrites a newer write, and that only one refresh runs per key?
answer_hinglish:
Dono guarantees ek idea se aati hain: refresh ek normal FLIGHT hai -- same `flights` Map, same version check -- koi alag mechanism nahi. PLAN.md: 'The refresh is an ordinary flight ... so it cannot overwrite a newer set / delete / clear, a dead-entry miss joins it, and one refresh at a time is the stage-1 single flight.'

Ek refresh per key: stale branch `if (!this.flights.has(key))` check karta hai. Pehli stale read flight register karti hai; baaki 49 concurrent stale reads flight dekh ke sirf purani value lete hain. Test: 50 concurrent stale reads -> loader 1 baar, `staleHits: 50, refreshes: 1, coalesced: 0`. Grace khatam hone ke baad koi miss aaye aur refresh abhi chal raha ho, toh woh usi flight mein JOIN karta hai (`coalesced` +1) -- doosra loader call nahi.

Newer write nahi overwrite: `set`, `delete`, `clear` sab `this.flights.delete(key)` (ya `flights.clear()`) karte hain -- running flight detach. Refresh jab resolve hota hai, `if (this.flights.get(key) === flight)` false hai, toh kuch store nahi. Flight object ki identity hi version hai -- projects/18-resilience ke breaker generations jaisa idea. Test teeno ke liye: set ke baad value 100 rehti hai, delete / clear ke baad undefined.

Teesra subtle point: refresh flight `waiters: 1` se start hoti hai -- cache khud ek waiter jo kabhi leave nahi karta. Kyun: grace ke baad ek caller join kare aur abort kare, toh `leave()` waiters 0 dekh ke refresh abort kar deta -- jo cache ne sabke liye start kiya tha. Mutations R6 (har stale read apna refresh), R8 (joiner refresh abort kar sake) aur F3 (version check hatao) pakde gaye.
why_needed: Background kaam aur foreground writes ke beech race ek classic cache bug hai: slow refresh purana data wapas likh deta hai. Version check usse structurally rokta hai.
real_world_analogy: Ghar ki diwaar paint karne ek painter bheja (refresh). Beech mein tumne khud naya paint kar diya (set). Painter aaya toh uske haath mein purana work order hai -- order register mein 'cancelled' hai, toh woh kuch nahi karta, bas chala jaata hai.
how_it_works: `startLoad` flight ko Map mein daalta hai; success par `flights.get(key) === flight` tabhi store. set / delete / clear flight Map se hatate hain. Stale branch running flight dekh ke naya start nahi karta. Refresh `waiters = 1`.
in_this_project: src/cache.ts `Flight<V>` interface ka comment ('The object itself is the key's load VERSION'), `startLoad()`, `leave()`, `set()` / `delete()` / `clear()`. `test/swr.test.ts`: '50 concurrent stale reads start ONE refresh and all get the old value', 'a miss after the grace ended while the refresh still runs JOINS the refresh', 'a caller that joins the refresh and aborts does NOT abort the refresh', aur describe 'a refresh never overwrites a newer write' (set / delete / clear). TwoLevelCache isi flight ke `isCurrent()` se Redis write bhi rokta hai.
advantages: Ek mechanism, do guarantees (single refresh + no stale write)
Koi version counter ya lock nahi: object identity
Joiner abort shared refresh ko nahi todta
disadvantages: Detached refresh ka kaam waste hota hai (loader chal chuka)
Stuck refresh (bina timeout) key ke saare future refreshes rok deta hai
Sirf in-process: doosre replica ke liye SET NX / tombstones chahiye
common_mistakes: Refresh ke liye alag Map / alag lock banana (race wapas)
Write ke baad running load ko detach na karna
Refresh ko caller-abortable banana
follow_up_questions: Why is object identity safer than a numeric version counter here?
How does TwoLevelCache extend this guarantee across replicas?
What if the refresh is detached but its value is newer than the set?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Refresh ko normal flight banana code reuse aur consistent semantics deta hai; badle mein refresh aur load alag policies (jaise alag timeout) nahi le sakte bina flight mein flag ke -- `refresh` flag already context mein hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Detach ke baad bhi loader chalta rehta hai (signal abort nahi hota jab tak waiters 0 na hon; refresh ka waiter cache khud hai) -- DB par ek bekaar query. Agar loader hang ho, flight Map mein rehti hai jab tak koi set / delete na kare.
advanced.alternatives: Per-key generation counter (number) jise load capture kare; compare-and-set on the entry; ya ek lock per key. Identity check sabse sasta hai aur counter overflow / map cleanup nahi chahiye.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Single process mein scale par koi issue nahi -- har check O(1). Multi-replica mein local version kaafi nahi: TwoLevelCache SET NX + tombstone + pub/sub invalidation (jo flight ko `l1.delete` se detach karta hai) laata hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Detach par loader ko abort signal dena jab koi asli caller wait na kar raha ho; refresh ke liye alag timeout; `refresh` duration ka metric; stuck flight detection (flight age > threshold par event).
